videos.title: Hundred Years' War: The Longest War in History
videos.description:
England and France hated each other for hundreds of years. So much that France almost disappeared. And it all happened because of the Hundred Years’ War. Three million people died in this war. At a time when England had only about five million people. Joan of Arc fought in this war. A girl who led an army at just 17 years old. This war was also the first in Europe to use cannons on a large scale. 

Today we will tell you how a simple fight over the throne turned into a long and brutal war. And how this war helped create two nations, the English and the French. We will tell the story of the Hundred Years’ War as if it happened YESTERDAY.

videos.title: The Most Terrifying Survival Story Ever
videos.description:
On October 13, 1972, a plane carrying the Old Christians rugby team crashed in one of the most remote parts of the Andes—the longest mountain range on Earth. On board were 45 people, stranded at an altitude of 3,600 meters. At night, temperatures here drop to -30°C. Just a few days later, the search was called off, even though most of the passengers were still alive. They had no food. No way to communicate with the outside world. And no hope of being rescued. Then, they were faced with a choice that would define them forever

videos.title: Fentanyl Is China's Revenge?
videos.description:
We’re diving into the Opium Wars — a conflict that dramatically changed the modern world in ways you probably don’t even realize. It all started with Britain’s obsession with Chinese tea. The problem was, the British had almost nothing to pay for it. So they came up with a cynical solution: they got China hooked on opium. That’s how Britain managed to drain the country of both its tea and its silver. Watch the full video to see how this wild story unfolded and how its consequences still echo across the world today. Let us know in the comments: did you know about these facts, or did something catch you by surprise?

videos.title: WWI: The Most Pointless War in History
videos.description:
1914. A world of grand empires, gleaming uniforms, and a fragile peace that shattered with a single bullet in Sarajevo. We call it “The Great War,” but the truth is darker: this was the war that made no sense. 

20 million lives lost — an entire generation wiped out — only for the world to stumble into an even deadlier nightmare just 20 years later. This is the story of how the modern world was forged in the blood-soaked trenches of the Somme and the poison clouds over Verdun.

It’s the terrifying leap from horses and bayonets to the birth of mechanical monsters: tanks, chemical weapons, and the dawn of total war.

videos.title: Why the Spanish Inquisition Was So Horrifying
videos.description:
The Spanish Inquisition – one of the darkest chapters of the Middle Ages. When we hear "Spanish Inquisition" we immediately picture horrifying torture, people burned at the stake, persecuted scientists, and women branded as witches during brutal medieval witch hunts.  

For centuries, the Spanish Inquisition has been accused of killing millions, plundering communities, and creating a living hell. The Catholic Church even issued a public apology for its role. But the truth is far more complicated than popular myths suggest. Let’s look at the facts: myth vs reality.

videos.title: Who Killed Princess Diana? (Full Documentary)
videos.description:
It’s 1995. Princess Diana — the most famous woman on the planet — sits down for a BBC interview that would change her life forever. In it, she boldly says her husband, Prince Charles, is not fit to be King of Great Britain. Just two years later, Diana dies in a tragic car crash. And soon after, the rumors start — people begin to whisper that her death… wasn’t an accident. Her marriage to Charles started like a real-life fairy tale: a dazzling gown, a royal carriage, thousands of guests. But how did that dream turn into a nightmare — one that ended with the death of the People’s Princess?

Today, I’ll break it all down. This is the story of Princess Diana — told as if it happened YESTERDAY.
